title: A derived custody summary is validated under typed-root premises the function's reported row does not grant
why: Measured by W47-TYPED-CONST-POINTER-VALUE (docs/reports/w47-typed-const-pointer-value/README.md, 'The two cascades'). W4 derives and validates a summary (legacy_summary::infer_cfg_summary) on a CFG built in an environment that does not yet hold the function's own contract, so protected_resource_formals protects none of its formals even though the validation run seeds the unresolved ones as entry-bound Owned resources. The typed reader's never-bound closure therefore treats a copy of such a formal (`const T *a = _a;`) as a root the body never binds, and the typed reads rooted there are admitted in the validation run. The reported run analyses the same body with the derived contract in force: the formals are protected, the copies are bound, and the same reads refuse. Instance: rd_kafka_topic_partition_cmp stays Unknown (IND at 21963, RET at 21967, unknown_alias _a/_b) while its summary (Owned, Owned, result none; reproduced in a fixture) validates, and rd_kafka_topic_partition_cmp_opaque moves Unknown -> Safe on it at this card's step 1. The summary is custody-correct for that body (it only reads), and every per-hop base obligation is still checked in the validation run; what differs is rule 5b's premise that a never-bound root reaches no tracked place, which is false there for a copy of an entry-seeded formal. The extent across the corpus (Safe functions whose same-unit callee has a validated summary but an Unknown row) is not measured. DISCHARGE: validation reads the typed-root premises with the same protected-formal set the reported run uses (or seeds a formal it binds as protected), with audited Lean and a measured corpus/system re-pin naming every Safe that moves; or a recorded decision, with the measured extent, that the validation run's premise is sufficient for the summary's claim.
